result:
Round 276 (SYS-5 stage 1) is implemented within the §5 grants. I'm raising one STOP for B on a single criterion (the disabled cursor, below); everything else is done and the tree is consistent. Nothing was committed or pushed, and no protected or frozen file was touched (manifest check rc 0; `git status` shows only §5 paths).

**What changed**
- **Seven transport buttons** (Undo, Redo, Split, Delete, Loop, Zoom to selection, Zoom back) no longer use native `disabled` when unavailable:
  - They get `aria-disabled="true"`; the attribute is absent when the button is available.
  - They stay in the Tab order, so the transport goes from 7 to 14 stops.
  - The first line of each click handler returns early, so a click or Enter on an unavailable button does nothing.
  - A mouse press on an unavailable button does not move focus.
  - The focus handoffs (Delete → Undo, Undo ↔ Redo, Zoom back → Fit) now key on `aria-disabled`.
- **Titles:** Undo, Redo, Split and Delete now state their reason (e.g. "Undo — nothing to undo yet (Ctrl+Z)"). Loop and the two zoom titles already had one and are unchanged.
- **Look:** the icon and label are dimmed instead of the whole button, so the focus ring stays at full strength. An unavailable button no longer shrinks when pressed.
- **Tailwind check:** the production build does produce the dimming rule (`:is(.aria-disabled\:\*\:opacity-40[aria-disabled=true]>*){opacity:.4}`), so that STOP condition did not trigger.
- **New doc:** `206-sys-5-disabled-reasons-stage-1.md`, with l.4 exactly as the task requires.

**Tests and checks run**
- The 20 §6.3 test files pass: 379 tests, slowest single test 1.49 s, nothing near 50 % of its timeout.
- typecheck, lint, Biome on the 7 owned files and `npm run build` all pass.
- Mutants M1–M5 each turn the expected rows red. M6 and M7 (deleting the Undo or Redo guard), added after the review, both turn SD2b red. Files were restored and hash-checked each time.
- SD5b was not written: no reachable state exists, since every handoff partner is available at the moment its source becomes unavailable. The per-pair reasons are in the report.
- My own Chromium probe at 1440 and 1280 (not C evidence) showed the 14 Tab stops, a full-strength ring, no hover or press change, children at 0.4 opacity, and no status change on click or Enter.

**STOP — needs B ruling: V-HOVER-SOFT `cursor: not-allowed`**
- The hover cursor on all seven reads `pointer`. The cause is app.css l.483 `button { cursor:pointer }`: it sits outside Tailwind's layers, so it beats the utility class.
- HEAD has the same result: an injected native disabled button with HEAD's own class also shows `pointer`. So this is not a regression.
- The fix needs l.483, which is outside the grant. Alternatively, B could allow the forced form `aria-disabled:cursor-not-allowed!`, a one-token change in the grant. I applied neither.

**Grant deviation, for B to classify**
- Two shared test constant groups are also used by Snap, Env, Master and Metronome tests, and those frozen components still use `enabled:` tokens: `BASE_FILL`, and `ON_TOKENS`/`DROPPED_TOKENS`.
- Rewriting them in place would have failed those tests. I added transport-only copies of the same length instead.
- The task's l.551–558 hint actually points at the Snap/Env assertions, so I left them unchanged.
- No assertion was removed.

**Code review (code-reviewer subagent, 8/10)**
- **Medium, fixed:** SD2 could not catch a missing Undo/Redo guard, because undo and redo on an empty history write no status. I added SD2b, which clicks all seven during an active pointer gesture, when those actions would otherwise write a refusal.
- **Low, not changed:** Delete's accessible name says "the selected clip" even when nothing is selected. §2.2 freezes that label; I propose it as `A-R276-REVIEW-DELETE-NAME`.
- **Low, fixed in doc 206:** two statements were imprecise (Space wording, and the untested partner-unavailable focus branch).
- **Low, noted for C:** clicking a greyed button no longer blurs a focused text field, so a marker rename or tempo field stays open. This is intended by §2.1; C may want one probe of it.
- **Architecture note, passed to B and not acted on:** the click guard is copied into seven handlers. For stage 2, the shared helper should own the click wrapper too.

Every browser and visual row (B-*, V-*, G276-AUTH, DOC-206, RT-FIX-276, STUDIO-SMOKE-276) is left to C. The full exact list is in the report.

Files are in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop/` (logs, probes and mutant scripts are in `a-round-276/`):
